allow_large: The owner asked on 2026-10-01 to fix hooks blocking every command for good; the shared launcher, both hosts' hook files, sync, doctor and their tests are one change (9 files)

amendments.because: The owner asked on 2026-10-01 to fix it for good: cover every common install folder and have doctor catch any machine where hooks still can't find forge
amendments.done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code find forge even when the hook's PATH lacks uv's tool folder: they add uv's default tool bin folder (XDG_BIN_HOME, else HOME/.local/bin) to the front of PATH before running forge, and still block (exit 2) when forge can't be found at all. A command-level test runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and a HOME whose .local/bin holds forge, and it runs; another with no forge anywhere still blocks. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.

amendments.because: The owner hit this on a fresh machine on 2026-10-01: with no forge installed, Forge's own hooks blocked every command, including the ones needed to install it; fix it for good
amendments.done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code find forge even when the hook's PATH lacks its install folder: before running forge they put UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR, XDG_BIN_HOME, HOME/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin (those that are set) in front of PATH, and still block (exit 2) when forge can't be found at all. forge doctor runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and reports, with the fix to apply, any that can't find forge. Command-level tests: each synced hook runs with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and forge under HOME/.local/bin, and under a UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR folder; with no forge anywhere it still blocks; doctor reports a hook that can't find forge. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.

amendments.because: Simplify a repeatedly reviewed area: the checkout-code fallback only served Forge's own repo, which the pinned-release fallback already covers, so it is dropped
amendments.done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code never leave a machine blocked just because forge isn't on the hook's PATH. In order they: run forge from PATH after putting UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR, XDG_BIN_HOME, HOME/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin (those that exist) in front; else, in Forge's own repo (repo = forge-source), run the checkout's code through uv; else, when uv is available, run the repo's pinned release through uvx (git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<pinned version>); else block (exit 2) with one plain line naming the install command for the pinned release and forge doctor, never a bare 'command not found'. forge doctor runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and reports any that can't run. Command-level tests: forge under HOME/.local/bin and under UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; no forge but uv present (runs the pinned release; uvx stubbed at its edge); Forge's own repo with no forge installed; nothing available (blocks with the plain line); doctor reporting a hook that can't run. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.

done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code never leave a machine blocked just because forge isn't on the hook's PATH. Through one shared launcher they: run forge from PATH after putting UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR, XDG_BIN_HOME, HOME/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin (those that exist) in front; else, when uv is available, run the repo's pinned release through uvx (git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<pinned version>); else block (exit 2) with one plain line naming the install command for the pinned release and forge doctor, never a bare 'command not found'. forge doctor runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, only after checking the launcher is exactly what sync writes, and reports any hook that can't run. Command-level tests: forge under HOME/.local/bin and under UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; no forge but uv present (runs the pinned release; uvx stubbed at its edge); nothing available (blocks with the plain line); doctor reporting a hook that can't run and refusing to run a launcher that differs from sync's. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.

findings.body: Claude's [hook contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#reference-scripts-by-path) documents that handlers run in the current directory, which follows `cd`. After Claude changes to a folder outside Git, `git rev-parse` fails and this command attempts to source `/.forge/hooks.sh`; the deny hook then exits 2 for every subsequent Bash command, including one to return to the project. Changing to another repository without the launcher has the same effect. Previously, the deny handler could check these commands without a repository root (`src/forge/deny.py:36–54`). Resolve the launcher from the host's stable project root instead of relying exclusively on the current directory. This directory-following behavior is new evidence not addressed by the shared-launcher ruling.
findings.title: Keep the launcher reachable after Claude changes directories

why: Codex runs its hooks with a PATH that lacks the folder uv installs forge into, so every hook command fails with 'forge: command not found' and the fail-closed deny hook blocks every shell command, even pwd, for a Codex orchestrator
